findings.title: All operations are valid declarative patches
findings.explanation: 3 operation(s) target allowlisted state paths with valid values and resolvable targets. No command strings detected.

findings.title: No resource is destroyed or replaced
findings.explanation: All 3 planned change(s) create or update resources in place.

findings.title: No protected resource is destroyed
findings.explanation: No plan entry destroys a resource carrying the "changesafe_protected" tag.

findings.title: Nothing to reverse
findings.explanation: The plan destroys nothing, so every change can be undone by reverting the code.

findings.title: No destructive change requires review context
findings.explanation: The plan destroys or replaces nothing, so there is nothing that requires a documented pull request review.

findings.title: Blast radius within limits (3 resources)
findings.explanation: Operations touch 3 resources (module-web-aws-autoscaling-group-app, module-web-aws-cloudwatch-metric-alarm-cpu-high, module-web-aws-security-group-rule-metrics-scrape), within the warning threshold of 15.

findings.title: No instruction-like language in the input
findings.explanation: No untrusted text supplied with this change attempts to issue instructions to the system.

skippedPolicies.because: a Terraform plan carries no inverse operations to verify; reverting means reverting the code, not replaying a patch

the proposal is derived mechanically from the plan with no model involved, so it can never declare its own precondition or postcheck steps; verification in this workflow happens through the pull request review instead
